title: The Bunker
tagline: Shelter K-7, 1983. The air is running out.
intro: November 1983. An inspection visit to fallout shelter K-7, forty metres beneath a forest in the East.
At 02:14, an alarm goes off. The airlock seals, the ventilation dies, the strip lights flicker. The staff are gone; there is only you, and what they left behind.
Forty-five minutes of air. Each of you searches a different room. Nobody gets out alone.
ending: The surface door gives way in a gust of icy air. Up above, the forest is quiet; it is snowing.
No one will ever know who set off the alarm. But now you know that Commander Orsini got out first, without warning anyone.
failEnding: The strip lights die one by one. The oxygen gauge drops into the red.
The rescue team will arrive at dawn. They will find your notes, scrawled on the walls. Try again.

zones.name: The locker room
flavor: A pair of wool socks, stiff with cold.
A shaving soap and a rusty razor.
A postcard from Saint-Malo, nothing written on the back.

zones.name: The commander's office
flavor: An ashtray full of Gitanes butts.
A photograph: a woman on a beach, 1961.
Paper clips, an eraser, a rubber stamp reading “SEEN”.

zones.name: The mess hall
flavor: A dented tin of corned beef, dated 1979.
This week's menu: “Monday: lentils. Tuesday: lentils.”

zones.name: The radio room
flavor: A pack of flat batteries, all dead.
A watch schedule: “Nobody between 1 and 2 a.m.” Someone has underlined it twice.

zones.name: The dormitory
flavor: A letter never sent: “Mum, everything's fine here.”
A harmonica, one tooth missing from the comb.

zones.name: The plant room
flavor: A blown fuse, blackened on one side.

blocks.text: The numbers mark the distribution valves.

Lay the overlay on the map, edge to edge.
Open the marked valves following the airflow: **from north to south**, one row after another. North is at the top of every map.

hints: The three sheets of the table fit together. One symbol is stained: its letter is missing, the lexicon will supply it.
The protocol requires reading the message starting from the last symbol received.
Read forwards, it gives ?ILTRE; the only lexicon word that fits is FILTRE (French for filter).
variants.solution: Symbols decoded backwards: ?ILTRE → lexicon = FILTRE

blocks.text: Short burst, emergency frequency. Operator's transcription (an oil stain hides one symbol):
Every RUBIS message is **sent backwards**: the first symbol received is the last letter of the word.
The resulting word opens the main filter.
